title: Google Cloud anchoring disqualifies Incentro despite good OSS posture and right size
content:
Incentro passes the criteria that usually matter most in this corpus: good open-source posture, the right size, and a Camunda practice that sits exactly where an append-only decision record attaches. It was dropped anyway, on the newer lens, because it is a Google Cloud partner serving customers from finance through to retail — cloud-anchored and commercially focused, which the assessment names as the opposite of local-first sovereign deployment.

The mechanism is about where a partner's architecture defaults live rather than which licence its tools carry. A firm whose delivery pattern assumes a hyperscaler will reach for managed services first; asking it to lead with client-owned infrastructure inverts the reference architecture it sells and the cloud-partner incentives attached to it. Open-source tooling on top of a hyperscaler is still not sovereign deployment.

The entry is explicitly labelled a clean example of the thesis doing real filtering work, and that is the reusable point. A screen that only ever confirms leads the previous criteria already liked is not filtering; this one removed a lead that scored well on size and posture, which is evidence the sovereignty criterion is load-bearing rather than decorative.
